title: Ride Sharing & Geospatial Dispatch (Uber)
intro: Design a real-time ride hailing and dispatch system tracking millions of moving driver locations and matching riders with sub-second latency.
objectives: Structure geospatial indexing using hierarchical spatial cells (Uber H3 / Google S2 / QuadTree).
Process high-frequency driver location heartbeats over persistent WebSocket/gRPC streams.
Execute optimal bipartite matching between riders and nearby drivers.
body:
### Geospatial Indexing: H3 Hexagonal Grid
Latitude/Longitude pairs cannot be queried efficiently with B-tree range queries ($O(N)$ table scans). Modern ride-sharing platforms discretize the Earth\'s surface into hierarchical spatial cells:
- **Uber H3**: Hexagonal hierarchical spatial index. Hexagons have the unique mathematical property that all 6 adjacent neighbors are equidistant, making radius and travel-distance calculations uniform.
- **Driver Location Updates**: Drivers emit location pings `(lat, lon, driver_id, status)` every 4 seconds. The dispatch engine maps `(lat, lon)` to an H3 cell index (e.g. resolution 8, ~460m across) and updates an in-memory spatial index (Redis Geospatial / memory table).
- **Nearby Driver Query**: `h3.kRing(riderCell, 2)` retrieves all adjacent cells within 2 rings, finding candidates in $O(1)$ time.
keyIdea: Discretize the globe into hexagonal cells (Uber H3). Route location pings into in-memory spatial indexes to evaluate nearby driver queries in O(1) time.

concepts.title: Bipartite Dispatch Matching
concepts.body: Batching ride requests every 5 seconds to solve global optimization (Hungarian algorithm) rather than naive greedy first-come matching.

concepts.title: Trip State Machine
concepts.body: Requested -> Matching -> DriverAssigned -> Arrived -> InTrip -> Completed.

examples: Uber Geospatial dispatching architecture running on custom H3 hex grids.

resources.title: H3: Uber's Hexagonal Hierarchical Spatial Index

quiz.prompt: Why are hexagonal cells (H3) preferred over square grid cells for geospatial dispatch?
options: All adjacent neighbor cell centers are equidistant in a hexagon grid, eliminating diagonal distance distortion
Square grids cannot cover curved terrain
quiz.explanation: In a square grid, diagonal neighbors are $\sqrt{2}$ times farther away. In a hexagonal grid, all 6 neighbors are strictly equidistant.
